chapters.title: What Is History?
chapters.tease: History turns scattered traces into stories we can test, argue over and learn from.

chapters.title: Primary and Secondary Sources
chapters.tease: Knowing who made a source, when and why is the first defence against being fooled about the past.

chapters.title: Archaeology: Reading the Ground
chapters.tease: Archaeology lets us meet the billions of people who never wrote anything down.

chapters.title: Stratigraphy: Layers of Time
chapters.tease: Stratigraphy turns a heap of earth into a calendar, read from the bottom up.

chapters.title: Radiocarbon Dating
chapters.tease: Radiocarbon gave the whole human past one timescale, from Ice Age caves to the first farms.

chapters.title: Tree Rings and Ice Cores
chapters.tease: Trees and ice keep yearly records that date ruins exactly and reveal the climate of the past.

chapters.title: Archives and Record Offices
chapters.tease: Archives keep the unique records that let us check what governments and people actually did.

chapters.title: Oral History and Memory
chapters.tease: Oral history keeps voices that never reach paper, and sometimes facts that are centuries old.

chapters.title: Forgeries, Hoaxes and Myths
chapters.tease: Exposing fakes keeps history honest, and the same tests now help us spot doctored photos and video.

chapters.title: Who Writes History?
chapters.tease: Who writes history decides whose lives are remembered, so every account must ask who is missing.

chapters.title: Before Writing: Tallies and Tokens
chapters.tease: Before anyone wrote a word, people cut notches and shaped tokens to remember numbers.

chapters.title: Cuneiform and the First Scribes
chapters.tease: The first writing kept accounts in wet clay, and its tablets survived for five thousand years.

chapters.title: Hieroglyphs and the Rosetta Stone
chapters.tease: A routine royal decree, copied in three scripts, let the world read ancient Egypt again.

chapters.title: The Alphabet's Long Journey
chapters.tease: A few dozen letters, first scratched by miners in Sinai, now write most of the world's languages.

chapters.title: Paper, from China to the World
chapters.tease: Cheap, light and easy to make, paper turned writing from a luxury into an everyday habit.

chapters.title: The Printing Press
chapters.tease: When copying became a machine job, ideas began to travel faster than any scribe could write.

chapters.title: Libraries, from Alexandria to the Archive
chapters.tease: Libraries turned private memory into public inheritance, and some outlived the empires that built them.

chapters.title: Calendars and the Counting of Days
chapters.tease: Calendars let societies plan harvests, festivals and debts, and turned the sky into a shared timetable.

chapters.title: Maps and the Shape of the World
chapters.tease: Maps let people claim land, cross oceans and picture a world far larger than anyone could walk.

chapters.title: Codes and Codebreakers
chapters.tease: Secret writing has decided plots, wars and elections, and now protects every online payment.

chapters.title: Barter, Debt and Gift
chapters.tease: Money grew from debts and gifts, not swaps: credit is older than cash.

chapters.title: The First Coins
chapters.tease: A stamp of guarantee let strangers trust metal without weighing it, and trade sped up.

chapters.title: Paper Money
chapters.tease: Paper let money outgrow metal, and let governments print, for better and for worse.

chapters.title: Banks and Bankers
chapters.tease: Banks turned idle savings into loans, and gave kings, merchants and states the power to borrow.

chapters.title: The Silk Roads
chapters.tease: A web of caravan routes carried silk, horses, religions and plague across Eurasia.

chapters.title: Spices and the Sea
chapters.tease: The hunt for pepper and nutmeg drove ocean voyages, trading empires and conquest.

chapters.title: Companies and Shares
chapters.tease: Shares let strangers pool money and limit risk, creating the modern corporation.

chapters.title: The Gold Standard
chapters.tease: Tying money to gold promised stability, but chained economies to a metal supply.

chapters.title: Crashes and Bubbles
chapters.tease: Boom and bust is the oldest rhythm in finance, and each crash rewrites the rules.

chapters.title: From Cards to Contactless
chapters.tease: Cards and phones turned money into messages, letting payments cross the world in seconds.

chapters.title: Walls and Fortifications
chapters.tease: Walls let farmers, cities and empires keep what they had built, and turned war into a contest of time.

chapters.title: The Horse in War
chapters.tease: For four thousand years the horse was the fastest thing in war: scout, transport and shock weapon in one.

chapters.title: Armour and the Knight
chapters.tease: Armour decided who survived a battle, and its cost helped create a warrior aristocracy.

chapters.title: Gunpowder Changes Everything
chapters.tease: Gunpowder made stone walls obsolete, armour optional and the state that could afford cannon supreme.

chapters.title: Navies and Sea Power
chapters.tease: Command of the sea decided where wars were fought, who could trade and which empires could last.

chapters.title: Sieges
chapters.tease: For most of history, war meant sieges: the fight for walled towns that held food, wealth and people.

chapters.title: Total War
chapters.tease: When whole nations were mobilised for war, every factory, farm and home became part of the battlefield.

chapters.title: Rules of War: from Chivalry to Geneva
chapters.tease: Rules of war turned mercy from a private virtue into public law, and atrocity into a crime with a name.

chapters.title: Spies and Intelligence
chapters.tease: Knowing an enemy's plans has won wars without a shot fired, and lost them when the spies were wrong.

chapters.title: Making Peace: Treaties and Truces
chapters.tease: Treaties turned victory and exhaustion into lasting rules, and the first ones were sworn before the gods.

chapters.title: Chiefs, Kings and Pharaohs
chapters.tease: Every state began with one question: who gives the orders, and why should anyone obey?

chapters.title: Hammurabi and the First Written Laws
chapters.tease: Carving laws in stone moved justice out of the ruler's head and into public view.

chapters.title: Democracy in Athens
chapters.tease: Athens showed that ordinary citizens, not kings or nobles, could make the big decisions.

chapters.title: The Roman Republic and Its Law
chapters.tease: Rome's checks on power and its written law became the template for half the world's courts.

chapters.title: Magna Carta
chapters.tease: Magna Carta put a king under the law, an idea later rebels and courts turned on every ruler.

chapters.title: Parliaments
chapters.tease: Parliaments turned the right to be consulted into the power to refuse a ruler money and laws.

chapters.title: Empires and How They Ruled
chapters.tease: Empires invented the tools of the modern state: provinces, censuses, post roads and civil servants.

chapters.title: Revolutions and Rights
chapters.tease: Revolutions turned favours granted by kings into rights owed to every human being.

chapters.title: Votes for All
chapters.tease: Universal suffrage made government answerable to everyone, not just to the rich and the male.

chapters.title: Courts, Juries and Police
chapters.tease: Courts, juries and police replaced the blood feud with rules, evidence and public judgement.

chapters.title: Ancient Healers
chapters.tease: Ancient healers turned private skill into written medicine that others could test, copy and teach.

chapters.title: The Four Humours
chapters.tease: The humours gave doctors one system to explain every illness, and kept bloodletting alive for 2,000 years.

chapters.title: Plague
chapters.tease: Plague emptied cities three times, reshaped economies and taught the world the idea of quarantine.

chapters.title: Anatomy and Dissection
chapters.tease: Looking inside the human body replaced ancient guesswork with a true map that all medicine now relies on.

chapters.title: Vaccination
chapters.tease: Vaccines turned killers like smallpox and polio into rarities and wiped smallpox from the Earth entirely.

chapters.title: Germ Theory
chapters.tease: Germ theory named the real enemies of health and made clean water, antisepsis and antibiotics possible.

chapters.title: Anaesthesia and Surgery
chapters.tease: Anaesthesia removed the pain and antisepsis the infection, making slow, careful and deep surgery possible.

chapters.title: Hospitals and Nursing
chapters.tease: Hospitals turned care for the sick from charity into a science, and nursing into a trained profession.

chapters.title: Antibiotics
chapters.tease: Antibiotics turned once-deadly infections into routine illnesses within a single generation.

chapters.title: Public Health: Sewers, Water and Clean Air
chapters.tease: Sewers, clean water and clean air saved more lives than any single medicine in history.

chapters.title: The Farming Revolution
chapters.tease: Farming fed far more people per acre, making towns, taxes and writing possible.

chapters.title: Bread and Grain
chapters.tease: Bread turned a hard, inedible seed into the everyday fuel of farmers, cities and empires.

chapters.title: The Plough and the Field
chapters.tease: Animal-drawn ploughs multiplied the land a family could farm and carved the shape of the countryside.

chapters.title: Salt, Sugar and Spice
chapters.tease: Small amounts of flavour drove taxes, monopolies, slavery and protest across five continents.

chapters.title: The Columbian Exchange
chapters.tease: The swap of crops, animals and diseases after 1492 rewrote diets, populations and landscapes worldwide.

chapters.title: Famine and Feast
chapters.tease: Feasts and famines reveal who holds power over food, and whether they share it.

chapters.title: Preserving Food: from Salting to the Fridge
chapters.tease: Preserved food let people survive winters, cross oceans, feed armies and live far from farms.

chapters.title: The Kitchen Through Time
chapters.tease: Where and how we cook shaped houses, family life, women's work and the shape of cities.

chapters.title: Clothes and Fashion
chapters.tease: Clothing let humans live in every climate, then became the world's most visible language of identity.

chapters.title: Home: from Longhouse to Semi
chapters.tease: The shape of the home records how families lived, worked, kept warm and shared space.

chapters.title: The First Cities
chapters.tease: Cities invented strangers, specialists, taxes and writing, and they appeared separately on four continents.

chapters.title: Pyramids and Monuments
chapters.tease: Monuments show what a society could organise: quarries, boats, food and thousands of hands, all aimed at forever.

chapters.title: Roman Engineering
chapters.tease: Rome standardised the arch, concrete, roads and aqueducts, and many of its lines still shape Europe's map.

chapters.title: Castles
chapters.tease: Castles turned a lord's home into a fortress, and stamped one family's power on the landscape for centuries.

chapters.title: Cathedrals
chapters.tease: Cathedrals pushed stone to its limits and turned walls into windows, using engineering learned by trial and error.

chapters.title: Bridges
chapters.tease: Bridges joined valleys, cities and markets, and taught engineers how stone, iron and steel really behave.

chapters.title: The Industrial City
chapters.tease: Factories pulled millions into crowded towns, and the crisis that followed invented modern public health and planning.

chapters.title: Skyscrapers
chapters.tease: Steel frames and safe lifts let cities grow upwards, putting thousands of workers on a single city block.

chapters.title: Planned Cities
chapters.tease: Planned cities show what rulers and reformers wanted society to look like, drawn as streets before anyone moved in.

chapters.title: Ruins and Rescue: Saving the Past
chapters.tease: Heritage rescue turned ruins into shared evidence, and every rescue forces a choice about what is authentic.

chapters.title: Roads
chapters.tease: Roads let rulers command, traders reach markets and ideas travel at the speed of a walking human.

chapters.title: Ships and Navigation
chapters.tease: Ships and the art of navigation turned oceans from barriers into highways for people, goods and ideas.

chapters.title: Canals
chapters.tease: Canals carried water to fields and boats over hills, feeding cities and powering early industry.

chapters.title: The Railway Age
chapters.tease: Railways shrank countries, created standard time and carried goods, armies and holidaymakers at unheard-of speed.

chapters.title: The Post
chapters.tease: Postal relays let empires govern at a distance; the cheap stamp let everyone write to everyone.

chapters.title: The Telegraph
chapters.tease: The telegraph cut communication free from transport, letting news cross oceans in minutes instead of weeks.

chapters.title: Telephone and Radio
chapters.tease: Telephone and radio carried the human voice across distance, reshaping private life, news and politics.

chapters.title: Cars and the Open Road
chapters.tease: The car made personal travel cheap and private, and in doing so it rebuilt cities, jobs and landscapes.

chapters.title: Flight
chapters.tease: Flight turned weeks of travel into hours, reshaping war, trade, tourism and how people picture the planet.

chapters.title: The Internet
chapters.tease: The internet joined the world's computers into one network, putting libraries, shops and conversations in every pocket.

chapters.title: Telling the Time
chapters.tease: Shared clock time let strangers meet trains, run factories and navigate oceans to the second.

chapters.title: Childhood and School
chapters.tease: Schooling for every child turned literacy from a scribe's secret into the default of modern life.

chapters.title: Work and Workers
chapters.tease: How people work decides how they live, where they live and how much power they have.

chapters.title: Slavery and Its Abolition
chapters.tease: The Atlantic slave trade moved millions in chains, and its abolition reshaped ideas of human rights.

chapters.title: Women's History
chapters.tease: Asking where the women were rewrote the history of work, family, religion and power.

chapters.title: Games and Sport
chapters.tease: Play reveals what societies valued, and written rules turned local games into global sports.

chapters.title: Festivals and Holidays
chapters.tease: Festivals turn the endless cycle of days into a shared story of belonging and memory.

chapters.title: Death and Remembrance
chapters.tease: How people treat their dead reveals their beliefs, their wealth and who they thought mattered.

chapters.title: Faith and Temples
chapters.tease: Temples were the most ambitious buildings of their age: storehouses, banks and landmarks as well as shrines.

chapters.title: History Now: The Past in the Digital Age
chapters.tease: Digital tools put the archive in everyone's pocket, and make checking sources more vital than ever.
